nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes: Entry point. The Angular app posts the ingredients and preferences here.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ recipes: $json.recipes, quota: { remaining: $('Use quota').item.json.remaining, limit: 3 } }) }}

nodes.name: Respond to Webhook
nodes.notes: Answers the app with the result.

nodes.name: Validate request
nodes.notes: Checks the request: 1 to 20 ingredients with a name of up to 40 characters, an amount and a known unit, portions 1-12, cooks 1-3, known cooking time, cuisine and diet.

nodes.name: Is valid?
nodes.notes: Splits the flow: valid requests continue, invalid ones get an error.

nodes.name: Respond with error
nodes.notes: Answers with status 400 and one clear message.

nodes.name: Read visitor address
nodes.notes: Reads the visitor address from the edge header, IPv4 or IPv6. Cloudflare overwrites that header, so it cannot be faked.

nodes.name: Use quota
nodes.notes: Counts this generation in the database: three per address and day, twelve per day in total.

nodes.name: Quota left?
nodes.notes: Stops the flow when the daily limit is reached.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ error: 'You have used all three recipes for today. Please come back tomorrow.' }) }}

nodes.name: Respond quota reached
nodes.notes: Answers with status 429 and tells the visitor when to come back.

nodes.name: Build prompt
nodes.notes: Turns the request into one order for the model, including the rules from the spec.

nodes.name: Ask the model
nodes.notes: Sends the order to the model and forces the answer into the agreed shape.

nodes.name: Recipe shape
nodes.notes: Forces the answer into the agreed fields, so the app always gets the same structure.

nodes.name: Check ingredient share
nodes.notes: Checks that every recipe uses at least 70 percent of the ingredients. Count of recipes and extras is already fixed by Recipe shape.

nodes.name: Rules ok?
nodes.notes: Splits the flow: a sound answer continues, a broken one ends with an error.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ error: 'The recipes could not be generated. Please try again.' }) }}

nodes.name: Respond generation failed
nodes.notes: Answers with status 502 when the model did not keep to the rules.

nodes.name: Build rows
nodes.notes: Turns the three recipes into database rows.

nodes.name: Save recipes
nodes.notes: Stores the recipes in the library and hands the saved rows back.

parameters.jsCode:
// The database hands the saved rows back, now with id and created_at.
const recipes = $input.all().map((item) => item.json).map((row) => ({
  id: row.id,
  createdAt: row.created_at,
  title: row.title,
  cuisine: row.cuisine,
  diet: row.diet,
  cookingTime: row.cooking_time,
  cookingMinutes: row.cooking_minutes,
  portions: row.portions,
  helpers: row.helpers,
  yourIngredients: row.your_ingredients,
  extraIngredients: row.extra_ingredients,
  steps: row.steps,
  nutritionPerPortion: row.nutrition_per_portion,
  nutritionTotal: row.nutrition_total,
  likes: row.likes,
}));

return [{ json: { recipes } }];

nodes.name: Collect saved recipes
nodes.notes: Reads the saved rows back into the shape the app expects, now with ids.

nodes.name: Refund quota
nodes.notes: Gives the generation back when the model or the database failed.

nodes.name: Groq Chat Model1
nodes.notes: The language model that writes the recipes. The API key stays in the credential.

nodes.name: Groq Chat Model
nodes.notes: Only runs when the answer misses the agreed shape, and rewrites it.
